value: Positions come from the data pilot spreadsheet (215 Ypres rows). British and French lines on 21, 23, 25, 29 and 31 October and 4, 9 and 11 November are read from the sketch maps of the British official history (1925); each holds until the next sketch or the next change in the text. Everything else, and every German position, comes from text: the first four days of the official history, the German General Staff account of 1917, two British histories of 1916 and encyclopedia articles. No French source was read. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.

value: The 1914 map is Sketch A of the British official history (1925). It is bound across two pages and about a kilometre is lost in the fold, so the current map shows through the gap. Sketch of the day puts the official history's own sketch for the date under the units, with its British (red), French (blue) and German (green) lines; there are eight, from 18 October to 11 November. Both are placed to within about 150 m. Use the Units button to read the sketch on its own. On a sketch's last date the British and French units should sit on its solid line. The sketches also draw the lines of the days before; those are not in the data.
